papers.title: Safeguarding the Eastern Himalayan Freshwater Ecosystems: An Integrated Biosecurity, Policy, and Community‐Led Framework to Prevent Invasive Fish Introductions in Northeast India
papers.authors: Shaikhom Inaotombi
papers.abstract: Freshwater ecosystems in the Eastern Himalayan Region of India—a global biodiversity hotspot—are threatened by invasive alien fish species perhaps facilitated by exotic aquaculture, the aquarium trade, climate change, and inadequate regulation. The invasion of alien species disrupts native biodiversity, causes ecological imbalances, and threatens livelihoods dependent on freshwater resources. To address this, the present study develops an integrated management framework by synthesizing and adapting global biosecurity protocols, policy tools, and community‐led conservation. The framework integrates three pillars: (1) advanced biosecurity, with real‐time monitoring and predictive modeling for early detection; (2) strengthened, context‐sensitive policies to regulate high‐risk species trade and aquaculture while respecting local economies; and (3) community empowerment through stewardship programs using traditional knowledge, sustainable livelihoods, and awareness. papers.title: Killing in the Pursuit of an Imaginary Order: A Critique of ‘Invasive Alien Species’ and ‘Pest’ Management
papers.authors: Núria Almirón, Sara Vidal-Ramón, Eze Paez
papers.source: OpenAlex / Enrahonar An international journal of theoretical and practical reason
papers.abstract: Contemporary management of invasive alien species and pests (IASP) relies on control and eradication strategies justified by the protection of biodiversity and ecological integrity. Yet these practices raise profound ethical concerns. This paper analyses the main instruments currently used in invasive species and pest management and develops a critique grounded in animal ethics and critical animal studies. It addresses the ethical paradoxes these interventions generate, their pragmatic limitations, and the political–economic structures that shape how harm and killing are justified and implemented. Through these analytical lenses, the paper questions whether invasion biology can claim moral justification while sustaining approaches that perpetuate species hierarchies and normalise violence against nonhuman beings in the pursuit of ecological order. Finally, the paper highlights the relevance of more compassionate and non-speciesist perspectives that seek to reframe conservation away from paradigms of control and toward coexistence.

papers.title: Monitoring farmland biodiversity using remote sensing
papers.authors: Caterina Barrasso, Stephanie Roilo, Antonia Dorea Ludwig, Vítězslav Moudrý, Jan Komárek
papers.source: OpenAlex / Burleigh Dodds series in agricultural science
papers.abstract: Monitoring biodiversity in agricultural landscapes is essential for addressing global biodiversity decline. Emerging remote sensing and artificial intelligence technologies enable large-scale, low-impact and cost-effective assessments. This chapter provides a concise review of remote sensing applications for farmland biodiversity monitoring, structured around the Essential Biodiversity Variable framework. We examine plants, animals, fungi and microorganisms, and their habitats in productive and semi-natural areas. Spaceborne and airborne sensors effectively assess agroecosystem structure and functioning, and detect plants and large mammals with distinct spectral or phenological traits. UAV imagery and camera traps offer higher resolution for monitoring smaller or cryptic species. Remote sensing also supports indirect methods, such as species distribution modeling, to infer the occurrence of species that are difficult to detect. Key challenges include technological, methodological and operational limitations. papers.title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning in agri-food systems: A comprehensive review of technological frontiers, socio-ethical barriers, and future roadmaps
papers.authors: Mohsen Abbod, Naser Safaie, Safaa N. Hussein
papers.abstract: Economic prosperity and human health heavily depend upon a stable food supply chain in agriculture. This essential network is fortified by modern farming techniques through boosted productivity and durability. Novel approaches are necessitated by the escalating worldwide need for nutrition. Consequently, agricultural practices and food security are positioned to be profoundly transformed by Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML). In this review, cutting-edge applications of AI in agriculture were investigated. A specific focus on precision crop management, optimized resource use, climate-resilient farming systems, and advanced livestock monitoring was undertaken. The article highlights how operational efficiency and decision-making are enhanced across all phases of any agricultural production system, such as planting, irrigation, pest control, harvesting, aquaculture, food safety, and post-harvest handling. This efficiency is attributed to the massive, heterogeneous datasets usually evaluated by AI frameworks to produce practical conclusions. papers.title: Translational Chemical Ecology: Bridging Mechanisms and Applications
papers.authors: Asim Munawar, Jamin Ali
papers.abstract: Understanding plant volatile chemistry is, in a very real sense, understanding how plants participate chemically in the living world around them . Translational chemical ecology explores how plants use volatile organic compounds (VOCs) as dynamic chemical signals that mediate interactions with insects, microbes, and neighbouring plants. It connects fundamental mechanisms of VOC biosynthesis, regulation, and ecological function with their translational potential in agriculture, biotechnology, and environmental resilience. This book integrates recent advances in molecular biology, omics technologies, and ecological modelling to demonstrate how plant volatiles can be harnessed for sustainable crop protection and smart farming systems. Designed for researchers, graduate students, and professionals in plant science, chemical ecology, and integrated pest management, this volume offers an interdisciplinary perspective linking basic mechanisms to real-world applications. Its clear organization and applied focus make it a valuable reference for understanding and utilizing the chemical language of plants in both natural and managed ecosystems.

papers.authors: T. Srinivasa Rao, D. Venkatarami Reddy, R. Erigela, B. Swetha, B. Balaji
papers.abstract: The growing challenges posed by rapid urbanization and increased vehicle density have highlighted the need for precise and privacy-preserving traffic flow prediction models. Traditional centralized learning methods involve aggregating privacy-sensitive traffic flow data, which poses severe privacy, scalability, and governance issues. To overcome these issues, this paper presents a disaster-aware privacy-preserving federated learning (PP-FL) solution for multi-city traffic flow prediction in heterogeneous and non-IID data settings. Each city separately trains a local deep learning model using local traffic, environmental, and disaster-related data, while only privacy-protected model updates are exchanged with a central aggregator. The proposed solution leverages secure aggregation and differential privacy to ensure data privacy and facilitate efficient cross-city knowledge sharing. Its frequent population outbreaks threaten the sustainability of alpine grasslands. Human activities and climate change may increase populations of grassland caterpillars and affect alpine plant communities. However, due to the rapid population turnover and significant fluctuations in their numbers, the relationship between grassland caterpillar population and plant community characteristics under grazing disturbance remains unclear. Based on our long-term experiment of grazing and enclosure in an alpine grassland on the eastern edge of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. We examined the effect of grazing disturbance on both caterpillar populations and alpine vegetation communities through detailed investigations of caterpillar counts and vegetation characteristics, combined with generalized linear mixed models (GLMM). papers.title: PCR-based assays for determining mating status in field-weathered Ceratitis capitata with enhanced precision across conventional, quantitative, and droplet digital platforms
papers.authors: José Marcelino, Cameron Zuck, Héctor Urbina, Matthew R. Moore, Matthew S. Siderhurst
papers.abstract: Accurately determining the mating status of the agricultural fruit fly pest Ceratitis capitata, commonly known as Medfly, is essential for timely and effective eradication efforts. To overcome the limitations of subjective DAPI-based staining assessments of females captured in dry Jackson traps and liquid Multilure traps, we developed a multi-tier molecular diagnostic method that unequivocally detects mating status using DNA probes targeting the male-specific Y114 locus on the Y-chromosome of C. capitata. Our protocol integrates morphological evaluation with increasingly sensitive molecular assays through the following steps: (1) A preliminary quality assessment of the specimens’ physical condition, DNA preservation, and mating status using conventional polymerase chain reaction (PCR) followed by agarose electrophoresis (cPCR); (2) quantification and real-time detection of sperm presence via quantitative PCR (qPCR); and (3) detection of trace amounts of sperm through droplet digital PCR (ddPCR). papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects over one-third of the global population, yet robust molecular biomarkers for early disease activity and treatment monitoring remain limited. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) carry nucleic acids, proteins, and lipids that reflect disease-associated intercellular signaling and are being investigated as liquid-biopsy analytes and therapeutic platforms. Candidate sEV miRNAs, proteins, and lipid signatures have shown potential for disease characterization, but evidence derives mainly from small, heterogeneous cohorts with limited external validation. No sEV-based assay is established for routine MASLD diagnosis, staging, or treatment monitoring. Mesenchymal stem cell-derived sEVs and engineered sEV platforms have shown therapeutic potential in preclinical MASLD-related models through modulation of inflammation, oxidative stress, lipid metabolism, and targeted cargo delivery, although some engineering strategies remain supported primarily by non-MASLD proof-of-concept evidence. papers.authors: Leopord Sibomana Leonard
papers.abstract: This study assessed the impact of leachate induced groundwater contamination near the Pugu Kinyamwezi dumpsite and associated pollution risks - the region's largest dumpsite by landmass and waste volume. Groundwater samples were collected from ten stations around the dumpsite, including one control station, with physicochemical parameters analyzed at Ardhi University’s Environmental Engineering Laboratory. Key parameters analyzed included pH, electrical conductivity (EC), total dissolved solids (TDS), major cations (Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, Na⁺, K⁺), anions (NO₃⁻, Cl⁻, SO₄²⁻, HCO₃⁻), and selected heavy metals (Fe, Mn, Zn, Pb, Cu). Aquachem modeling was used to assess water types and hydrochemical evolution. The results revealed that most groundwater samples met East African Standards (EAS 12:2018) and WHO drinking water standards. papers.title: Farmland biodiversity monitoring in Europe: Germany
papers.authors: Christian Levers, Damien Finn, Sebastian Klimek, Demetra Rákosy, Wiebke Sickel
papers.source: OpenAlex / Burleigh Dodds series in agricultural science
papers.abstract: Germany lacks a standardised and coordinated farmland biodiversity monitoring framework. However, several independent and heterogeneous programmes generate datasets for farmland-related biodiversity assessments. These programmes have limitations, including limited taxonomic coverage, lack of long-term trends, and insufficient data on agricultural land use/management, affecting the early detection of declining ecosystem conditions. MonViA, launched in 2019, is a nationwide, representative, and science-based framework that addresses key gaps in farmland biodiversity monitoring, aiming to develop monitoring concepts and indicators for agri-environmental policy for Germany. MonViA complements existing monitoring programmes with its farmland focus, national-level indicators on habitat, species, and genetic diversity, and modular design. The chapter outlines key steps towards an integrated farmland biodiversity monitoring in Germany through improved survey designs, novel survey methods, and advancements in data management, access, and integration. papers.abstract: The efficiency of honey production in apiaries depends largely on the work capacity and health of the bees in charge of this activity. Sanitary management in apiaries and hives is not entirely effective, revealing that the chemicals used can affect the behavior of workers, reduce their immunological capacity, and compromise the quality of the honey. The lack of alternative treatments and the lack of available information on natural products makes it important to search for less harmful solutions that are accessible to honeybee producers. The objective of this study was to determine the existing problems in apiaries in Soconusco, Chiapas. After conducting interviews and inspecting the apiaries, samples were taken from infected and uninfected apiaries and analyzed with ADP medium in the laboratory to identify the fungi causing the problem in the production boxes. These fungi were analyzed using a lactophenol blue staining technique under a microscope. papers.title: Integrated Ecological Strategies for the Management of Fruit Flies (Bactrocera dorslis spp.) in Citrus Agroecosystems
papers.authors: Azeem Maqsood, Muhammad Talha Bin Zahid, Hafiz Muhammad Usman, Waqar Sattar, Umer Raza
papers.abstract: Fruit flies (Bactrocera dorsalis spp.) represent one of the most destructive pest complexes in citrus agroecosystems, causing severe yield losses, quality deterioration, and restrictions on international market access. Their polyphagous nature, high reproductive potential, and strong adaptability make management particularly challenging under tropical and subtropical conditions. Excessive reliance on synthetic insecticides has led to environmental contamination, disruption of natural enemies, pesticide resistance, and food safety concerns, necessitating the adoption of sustainable alternatives. This review synthesizes integrated ecological strategies for the effective management of fruit flies in citrus production systems, with an emphasis on reducing chemical dependence while maintaining effective pest suppression. The paper examines the biology, ecology, population dynamics, and damage mechanisms of Bactrocera spp., highlighting key drivers influencing infestation patterns. papers.title: Utilizing the invasive fruitwood Pyrus calleryana as substrate for mushroom cultivation, an experimental study in practical sustainability
papers.authors: Matthew D Helton
papers.source: OpenAlex / UTC Scholar (University of Tennessee at Chattanooga)
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility of using woodchips from the invasive Pyrus calleryana (Callery pear) as substrate for mushroom cultivation. Pleurotus ostreatus, Hericium erinaceus, and Ganoderma lucidum were grown on a pear wood substrate and on a conventional oak substrate to compare, yield, sensory attributes, and metabolite production. P. ostreatus showed no significant differences in yield or biological efficiency (p > 0.05), only sweetness (p = 0.022) differed significantly. H. erinaceus yield and efficiency were similar (p > 0.05), with greater second-flush yields in oak controls (p = 0.034) but no sensory differences (p > 0.05). G. lucidum performance was comparable across treatments (p > 0.05), yet triterpenoid content was reduced in pear substrates (p = 0.031). Results indicate P. calleryana biomass can sustain edible mushroom production without affecting yield or quality, while substrate composition influences bioactive metabolite synthesis, supporting invasive biomass valorization as a sustainable management strategy.

papers.authors: Phillip Joschka Haubrock, Teun Everts, Ronaldo Sousa, Janeide de Assis Guilherme Padilha, Ismael Soto
papers.abstract: The management of biological invasions is increasingly characterised by a sequence of incremental wins and recurring management losses, whereas invasion pressure, ecological impacts, and socio-economic costs continue to rise globally. Here, we propose that this pattern reflects systemic constraints in post-introduction management, rather than a lack of effort, knowledge, or intent. We conceptualise invasion outcomes as the joint product of non-native species' impacts and spread and propose that these dimensions are intertwined and context-dependent, ultimately showing that this view can help explain why many management actions tend to fail at larger spatial scales. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. papers.abstract: Natural rubber is a strategic non-oil and gas commodity for Indonesia, acting as a crucial pillar for the national trade balance and the socioeconomic livelihoods of millions of smallholder farmers. However, its export value has exhibited extreme volatility over the past three decades, creating macroeconomic vulnerabilities and threatening rural incomes. This study aims to analyse the short-term and long-term determinants of Indonesia’s natural rubber export value from 1994 to 2024. Using annual time-series data, this research evaluates four key variables: world rubber price (RSS3), Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER), domestic rubber production, and Foreign Direct Investment (FDI). The Error Correction Model (ECM) was employed to disentangle transient short-run dynamics from long-run equilibrium paths. The empirical results reveal that world rubber price (RSS3) and domestic production exert significant positive effects on export value in both the short and long term. papers.abstract: Phyllophaga sp. is a pest that causes various types of damage to crops and economic losses. One control alternative is biological control, such as the use of entomopathogenic fungi that cause infections and death in various insects of economic interest. The objective of this research was to molecularly identify three strains of the entomopathogenic fungus Metarhizium, select those with the greatest pathogenic capacity against white grubs [Phyllophaga sp.], and with viability for mass reproduction and formulation as a bioinsecticide. The three strains belong to the species M. anisopliae, with strains Ma70 and Ma2 showing greater pathogenicity. They were reproduced in vitro and in rice to determine their commercial potential. Conidia production by both strains [2–3 × 10⁸] was lower than the target production [1 × 10¹⁰]; therefore, future research should focus on increasing conidia production in solid substrates.

papers.authors: Mohamed Alnuaimi
papers.source: OpenAlex / Emirati Journal of Education and Literature
papers.abstract: Date palm (Phoenix dactylifera L.) cultivation in the Arabian Peninsula represents a six- millennium agronomic tradition now undergoing rapid genomic and phytochemical reappraisal. This Review synthesises advances across cultivar genomics, salinity tolerance, pest and disease biology, fruit phytochemistry and clinical evidence, while subjecting methodologically contested domains to critical appraisal. Whole-genome resequencing, long-read assemblies and the recent telomere-to-telomere Ajwa reference have clarified domestication pathways, two-subpopulation structure with substantial Phoenix theophrasti introgression into North African cultivars, and the genetic architecture of fruit colour and sugar composition through VIRESCENS and linked invertase loci. Functional validation of candidate genes for sex determination, salinity tolerance and pest resistance nonetheless remains conspicuously absent, and quantitative trait loci for yield, salinity and Bayoud resistance are unmapped. papers.authors: , Azam Mahdipour, Mojgan Zaeimdar, , Mohammad Sadegh Sekhavatjou

papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: This study aimed to investigate the concentrations of heavy metals bound to airborne Particulate Matter (PM) in high-traffic districts of Tehran, Iran, and to determine the carcinogenic risk and Hazard Quotient (HQ) of these metals using a descriptive-applied method. Methods: Six indoor/outdoor stations were established in three high-traffic districts of Tehran. Each station was sampled with six replicates in winter 2018 (36 samples in total). After extracting the metals from fiberglass filters by acid digestion based on the ASTM (the American Society for Testing and Materials method), the concentrations of heavy metals were determined by an Inductively Coupled Plasma (ICP-OES) device. The human health risk was evaluated according to the US EPA (Environmental Protection Agency) standard method. The obtained data were analyzed by the Spearman correlation and Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANOVA) in SPSS. papers.title: Rational design of novel benzisothiazolinone derivatives as antivirulence candidate for management of plant bacterial diseases
papers.authors: Jia‐Rui Rao, Zhi‐Jun Luo, Lei Liu, Pan Xu, Tai‐Hong Zhang
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Chemical bactericides remain a major tool for the control of plant‐pathogenic bacterial diseases. Although 1,2‐benzisothiazol‐3(2 H)‐one (BIT) exhibits potent antibacterial activity, concerns over its cytotoxicity and ecotoxicity constrain its agricultural application. This study aimed to develop BIT ‐based analogues to elucidate their initial antibacterial mechanism while reducing toxicity. RESULTS In this work, 39 benzisothiazolinone analogues functionalized with an isopropanolamine linker were synthesized and biologically evaluated. Compound A12, bearing a 4‐trifluoromethylbenzylamino group, emerged as the lead candidate. Although less active than BIT, A12 displayed median effective concentration (EC 50) values of 3.36 and 4.87 μg mL –1 against Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo) and Xanthomonas. axonopodis pv. citri (Xac), respectively, outperforming bismerthiazol (BT) and thiodiazole copper (TC). Compared with BIT, A12 showed lower cytotoxicity across four human cell lines, and lower toxicity towards zebrafish, earthworms and rice seedlings. papers.abstract: Andisols are known to hold the highest soil carbon stocks among mineral soil types; they are generally found in highlands, fertile, and suitable for vegetable horticulture. Cultivation practices can deplete soil organic matter, thereby reducing carbon stocks and soil fertility. This study aims to examinethe impact of land-use intensity and its management in vegetable cultivation on surface carbon stocks and fertility status of Andisol in the Kayu Aro Barat District, Kerinci Regency. A survey method was employed, with observation points and soil samples selected via purposive random sampling. Soil surface carbon stock were estimated using data on soil organic carbon, bulk density, and soil volume at a depth of 0-30 cm. Soil fertility was assessed based on organic carbon concentrations and chemical properties, following the Technical Guidelines for Soil FertilityEvaluation from the Bogor Soil Research Institute. It has the effects of clearing heat and detoxifying, relieving pain, promoting blood circulation, and reducing swelling. As a highly valued traditional Chinese medicine, it contains a variety of chemical components. Among them, oridonin (ORI) exhibits antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer properties, garnering significant attention in pharmacological research. Furthermore, ORI serves as a crucial quality control marker for I. rubescens. To improve the efficacy and safety of its applications and ensure that the isolated monomer compounds exhibit high purity and favorable stability, the extraction and purification processes have been optimized. Synthetic ORI-derived products exhibit anti-inflammatory and antibacterial activities, which are widely used as dietary supplements and functional beverages in daily life. papers.title: Evolution of Food Science: Bridging Tradition and Innovation
papers.authors: Ranjana Chand, Shubham Kaintura
papers.source: OpenAlex / International Journal of Research and Review
papers.abstract: Food science has evolved from indigenous culinary wisdom and ancient preservation methods into a complex interdisciplinary field that integrates modern technological advancements, systems biology, and data analytics. This transformation reflects a continuous interplay between traditional knowledge systems and cutting-edge scientific innovation aimed at addressing contemporary global challenges including nutrition security, public health, and environmental sustainability. This chapter comprehensively examines the historical foundations of food science, its scientific milestones, and contemporary innovations such as biotechnology, nanotechnology, and personalized nutrition. Further, it highlights integrative approaches that meld traditional practices with novel technologies, supported by illustrative case studies. Ethical considerations surrounding intellectual property and cultural stewardship are discussed alongside future directions emphasizing systems thinking, resilience, and equity. This synthesis articulates a pathway toward sustainable, ethical, and health-promoting food systems at the nexus of tradition and innovation. Keywords: food science, traditional knowledge, food inno

papers.authors: Workneh Ayall Negash
papers.abstract: Access to quality water is critical for public health; however, Ethiopia is grappling with challenges stemming from inadequate infrastructure and limited resources. This study evaluated the quality of drinking water sourced from large and medium-sized pump-based systems in Central Gondar, comparing the findings against WHO water quality standards. Employing an explanatory mixed methods research design, 415 respondents were selected through systematic sampling. Data were gathered through surveys, focus groups, and key informant interviews, alongside experimental analyses conducted at sample sites. The results indicated a low level of satisfaction with drinking water quality, with only 1.3% of householders reporting very high satisfaction and 18% expressing satisfaction. Regarding water treatment, a mere 0.26% of households were very satisfied, while 53% voiced dissatisfaction, underscoring concerns about the effectiveness of treatment methods. Additionally, approximately 55% of respondents rarely observed changes in water quality due to seasonal variations, reflecting a limited understanding of safety testing protocols. papers.title: Autonomic nervous system as a key modulator in stress-related inflammatory bowel disease: Mechanisms and therapeutic implications
papers.authors: Xin-Xin Hu, Xue-ping ZHANG, Cheng-Xiang Wang, Rui-Rong Yang, Li-Xin Ma
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic inflammatory intestinal disorder affecting more than 7 million people worldwide, with a growing global burden. Psychological stress may aggravate intestinal inflammation by disrupting autonomic nervous system (ANS) balance. This review considers the contribution of the ANS to stress-related IBD. Sympathetic and vagal pathways can exert distinct effects on intestinal barrier integrity, immune responses, and inflammatory activity through neurotransmitters and neuroimmune signaling. We also explore ANS-targeted therapies, such as β-blockers and vagus nerve stimulation, as potential precision interventions for IBD.

papers.title: Gut microbiota signatures in colorectal cancer: Evidence synthesis from umbrella review and probiotic intervention studies
papers.authors: Li-Xuan Zeng, Yu-Chen Jiang, Yi-Qing Wang, Fei Ye, Yue Ouyang
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Aberrant alterations in the gut microbiota have been widely reported in colorectal cancer (CRC), but taxon-level associations remain heterogeneous in direction, magnitude, and reproducibility across studies. AIM To conducted an umbrella review with a second-order meta-analysis to identify reproducible CRC-associated taxa and to summarize gut microbiota changes after probiotic or synbiotic interventions. METHODS We included eligible meta-analyses of CRC-associated gut microbiota and evaluated them using AMSTAR 2 (a measurement tool to assess systematic reviews). After standardizing effect sizes and deriving missing standard errors, we performed a second-order meta-analysis to estimate pooled effect sizes, 95% confidence intervals (CIs), P values, and heterogeneity. Candidate taxa were identified using predefined criteria, and species-level findings were mapped to genera. We also added original CRC studies on probiotics and synbiotics, assessed bias using RoB 2, and combined the data via standardized mean differences (SMDs), wherever appropriate. papers.title: Dietary Isoflavonoids and Brain Tumors: Unlocking Neuroprotective Potential, Molecular Mechanisms, and Novel Therapeutic Avenues in Neuro-Oncology
papers.authors: Mohsen Akbaribazm
papers.abstract: Brain tumours, particularly Glioblastoma (GBM), remain among the most aggressive malignancies because of profound molecular heterogeneity, Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB)-restricted drug delivery, therapeutic resistance, and an immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment. Naturally occurring dietary isoflavonoids, including genistein, daidzein, biochanin A, formononetin, glycitein, and the metabolite equol, have emerged as promising multitarget phytochemicals with potential applications in neuro-oncology. This review comprehensively summarises current evidence regarding the molecular mechanisms, pharmacokinetic characteristics, preclinical efficacy, translational advances, and emerging therapeutic applications of dietary isoflavonoids in brain tumour prevention and treatment, with particular emphasis on glioblastoma. A narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science to identify English-language studies published between 2000 and 2025. Experimental investigations, clinical studies, systematic reviews, and relevant regulatory reports were critically evaluated. papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Intelligent Systems and Internet of Things
papers.abstract: The integration of Internet of Things (IoT) into agriculture is increasingly transforming conventional farming practices into intelligent, connected, and data-driven systems, offering opportunities to enhance productivity, and resource-use-efficiency and promote sustainable food security. This study presents a comprehensive systematic literature review of IoT-based smart agriculture, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA 2020) framework. A total of 203 peer-reviewed publications between 2020-2024 were systematically reviewed to examine three interconnected dimensions; IoT technologies, agricultural applications, and implementation barriers. The technological analysis covers sensing technologies, embedded controllers, commu-nication protocols, and computing architectures with particular attention to programmable logic controllers (PLCs), ESP32, microcontrollers, and Raspberry Pi platforms, wireless sensor networks, long range wide area network (LoRaWAN), NB-IoT, Zigbee, and cloud, edge, and hybrid computing architectures in supporting data processing, intelligent analytics, and real-time decision-making approaches. papers.title: Regulatory Provisions for Introducing Phytopharmaceutical Drugs in Indian Market
papers.authors: Anshita Anshita, Anshu Dalal, GOBIND YADAV, Arun Nanda
papers.abstract: Plants have been recognized as a very useful and important source of drugs, since time immemorial. However, in the present day, context, usefulness of plants has been questioned, on the grounds of quality control, lack of clinical trials, etc. Historically, plant drugs listed in "Official books" under "Schedule I" of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, were accepted for marketing in India, without any need for clinical trials. However, such drugs, although marketed in India, could not be marketed as "drugs" in countries like USA, EU, Japan, China, etc., wherein these drugs failed to meet the same standards of quality, consistency and clinical evidence, as chemical drugs. Thus, several Indian "drugs" were introduced in US market as "dietary supplements". This article discusses the concept of "phytopharmaceuticals", as introduced by amendment in the Indian Act, in 2015. The legal provisions related to Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani drugs, in India, are traced out. papers.title: Morphological and physiological responses to water stress and potassium nutrition in Eucalyptus grandis Hill Ex Maiden seedlings
papers.authors: LA Urriola, PL Fernández, AM Lupi
papers.abstract: In this study, the response of Eucalyptus grandis seedlings to varied water availability and potassium fertilization in coarse-textured soil was investigated. The experiment took place in a greenhouse in Buenos Aires, Argentina, over 56 days, with 15 replicates for each treatment. We maintained pots in the non-water-limited group at field capacity (FC), while those in the water-restricted group were maintained at 40% FC. Each water regime received one of three potassium levels (K1, K2, and K3). We measured plant height and root-collar diameter periodically. At the end of the experiment, biomass allocation among plant parts was quantified. We also evaluated physiological traits by measuring stomatal conductance and relative water content (RWC). The results show that potassium fertilization did not improve seedling performance under water stress or enhance growth in well-watered seedlings. Water restriction was the main limiting factor. Keeping soil moisture at 40% of FC reduced height growth, root-collar diameter, biomass, and leaf area. It also negatively affected physiological traits such as stomatal conductance and RWC, but did not cause seedling mortality.

papers.title: Phytochemical profile and pharmacological applications of Silybum marianum (L.)
papers.authors: Maria-Larisa Ardelean (căs.Rusu), Romeo Teodor Cristina, Mihai Folescu, Флорин Муселин, Alexandru O. Doma
papers.source: OpenAlex / Romanian Journal of Veterinary Sciences
papers.abstract: Silybum marianum L., a member of the Asteraceae family, is one of the most valuable medicinal plants, highly regarded for its abundance of bioactive compounds and diverse pharmacological applications. Native to the Mediterranean region, the species has spread globally, demonstrating remarkable ecological adaptability and resistance to unfavourable pedoclimatic conditions. The main phytochemical constituent, silymarin, is a complex of flavonolignans predominantly silibinin, isosilibinin, silychristin, and silydianin, which exhibit potent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and hepatoprotective properties. In addition to these compounds, the plant contains phenolic acids, flavonoids, unsaturated fatty acids, proteins, and fibres, all contributing to its high therapeutic and nutritional value. Silymarin acts by stabilising hepatocyte membranes, inhibiting toxin penetration, and stimulating cellular regeneration, while also exhibiting antidiabetic effects through enhanced insulin sensitivity and antitumoral activity via the induction of malignant cell apoptosis. papers.title: Environmental control in next-generation plant factories
papers.authors: Toyoki Kozai, Hiroko Nakaoka, Na Lu, Duyen T. P. Nguyen, Yuxin Tong
papers.source: OpenAlex / Burleigh Dodds series in agricultural science
papers.abstract: This chapter explores ways of optimizing environmental control of cultivation rooms (CRs) in next-generation plant factories. After considering design issues for CRs, the chapter focuses on measurement, analysis and control of three-dimensional (3D) distributions of environmental variables within a leaf canopy and root zone of a plant community in a CR. As the chapter shows, major productivity improvements can be achieved by optimally controlling the 3D environment and the interaction of the environment with the phenotype.

papers.title: Emerging Opportunities in Multimodal Artificial Intelligence Phenotyping for Insect‐Resistance Crop Breeding
papers.authors: Kusuri Karthik, Podishetti Shiva Krishna, Abhishek Ganugapati, Monoj Sutradhar
papers.abstract: Breeding insect‐resistant cultivars depends on phenotypes precise and heritable enough to resolve the genetic variation underlying resistance. The ordinal damage score, recorded at a single timepoint, compresses antixenosis, antibiosis and tolerance into one number and may therefore limit the resolution of QTL mapping and GWAS. This review evaluates multimodal artificial intelligence (AI), the joint analysis of imaging, behavioural and physiological data streams, as a route to mechanism‐resolved resistance phenotypes. Three questions frame the synthesis: whether multimodal AI can generate more precise insect‐resistance phenotypes; whether such phenotypes are heritable, repeatable and suitable for genetic mapping; and how they could be integrated into breeding decisions. The evidence to date is largely unimodal, coming from damage segmentation, electrical penetration graph (EPG) waveform classification and physiological imaging studied separately, and no study has yet compared multimodal and conventional phenotypes in the same insect‐resistance mapping population. papers.title: Misidentification has obscured the wider distribution of the land snail Oxychilus translucidus (Mortillet, 1853) in Europe (Gastropoda: Oxychilidae)
papers.authors: Louis Bronne
papers.abstract: The spread of alien species may remain undetected when they are misidentified as morphologically similar taxa. The land snail Oxychilus translucidus (Mortillet, 1853) provides a striking example of this phenomenon. We demonstrate that its distribution has been substantially underestimated because populations have been confused with other Oxychilus species. New records from Belgium and southern Spain, confirmed using shell morphology, genital anatomy and mitochondrial COI sequences, include the first outdoor population known from Western Europe. Re-examination of earlier material further revealed overlooked Belgian records and showed that recently published Italian greenhouse populations identified as Oxychilus alliarius (Miller, 1822) also belong to O. translucidus. By compiling 152 accepted occurrence records from the literature, citizen-science platforms and original observations, we reconstruct the species’ distribution from the Iberian Peninsula to the Russian Far East. papers.title: Plant pathogenic continuum in the microbiome era
papers.authors: Iva Rosić, Tanja Berić, Slaviša Stanković, Ivan Nikolić
papers.abstract: Plant pathology has traditionally relied on a binary distinction between pathogens and non-pathogens, or between harmful and beneficial microorganisms. However, this distinction is becoming increasingly difficult to maintain in the microbiome era. For many plant-associated microorganisms, pathogenicity is not a fixed property but varies along a gradient depending on host physiology, microbial strain, environmental conditions, resident microbiota, and time. This review discusses a plant pathogenicity continuum as a framework for interpreting this fluidity. Within this continuum, we discuss four interconnected positions: true or near-deterministic pathogens, context-dependent pathogens, opportunistic pathogens, and pathobiome- or dysbiosis-associated disease states. These positions should not be treated as rigid categories, but as reference points that help compare how strongly disease depends on the host, environment and microbiome interactions. We also discuss the strain-level problem in plant pathology, because species or pathovar-level detection often does not capture real differences in virulence and host range. papers.title: From shade to sustenance: tree species in home and domestic gardens
papers.authors: Lucian Dincă, Cristinel Constandache, Adrian George Peticilă, Iulian Alexandru Bratu, Gabriel Murariu
papers.abstract: Introduction Home and domestic gardens are multifunctional systems that support biodiversity, food security, sustainable resource use, and human well-being. However, a comprehensive synthesis of tree species associated with these gardens and their ecological and socioeconomic contributions remains necessary. This review aimed to characterize research trends and synthesize the available evidence on tree species in home and domestic gardens worldwide. Methods A two-stage approach was applied, combining bibliometric analysis of publications retrieved from the Scopus and Web of Science databases for the period 1978–2024 with a qualitative review of the identified literature. The bibliometric dataset comprised 486 records. The qualitative synthesis examined four thematic areas, including tree species diversity, their uses, and their contributions to ecosystem services. Results Scientific publications increased steadily from 2015 onward, reaching a peak in 2021. The United States, India, and Ethiopia were among the leading contributors to research in this field.
